critical_steps: Both source families are Parseval because their squared energies integrate to the scalar norm squared.
Their analysis ranges coincide in the L2 coefficient Hilbert space, so weak disjointness fails.
The singleton modification makes the literal pointwise combined kernel trivial.
The combined analysis operator nevertheless has a nonzero kernel because its value is zero almost everywhere.
Replacing pointwise zero by almost-everywhere zero is equivalent to trivial intersection of the two analysis ranges.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact scalar continuous g-frame construction on Lebesgue measure plus an analysis-operator kernel equivalence.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest reformulation of other disjointness notions is asserted.

limitations: The finding corrects only Theorem 2.2(v) under its literal pointwise quantifier.
If the source intended the displayed pointwise condition as shorthand for almost-everywhere equality, the repaired theorem is the intended statement and the defect is quantificational.
No claim is made about parts (i)--(iv) of Theorem 2.2.

title: A null-set defect in the weak-disjointness criterion for continuous \(g\)-frames
